thermonuclear-code-quality finding 1 (blocking in its report) asked for the allowance to move to DepsInput.SuggestionTimeout -> NewDeps -> Deps, as DepsInput.StreamHeartbeat does. Rejected: the architect settled this against code before implementation (dispatch://INFRA-56/comment/a638b06a-598d-4f37-a892-719e97ec5762) and the departure is deliberate - an exported Deps field would let a caller outside the package change the 300 ms that cmd/dispatch/README.md and CHANGELOG.md promise unconditionally, which is the one thing this issue must not do. The hazard the finding names (three construction sites can disagree) is real and is what the pin test patrols; I measured the pin catching it.

thermonuclear-code-quality finding 2 called TestTheDeploymentsSuggestionAllowanceIsTheDocumentedBound tautological and asked for a bare 'writeSuggestionTimeout != 300*time.Millisecond' instead. Rejected on measurement: with register (server.go:325) drifted to &server{deps: deps, suggestionTimeout: 5 * time.Second} through a Go -overlay that left the workspace untouched, the test as written FAILs with 'the server a deployment runs allows 5s for its suggestions, want 300ms as cmd/dispatch/README.md and CHANGELOG.md promise', while a constant-only pin would stay green. Reviewer's own run, 2026-10-25T01:28Z; jj diff --stat empty after it.

thermonuclear-code-quality finding 3 asked for the 1 ns subtest to be deleted as duplicating TestComputeAndPersistSuggestionsRespectsDeadlineWhenProjectLookupIsLocked. Rejected: that sibling calls computeAndPersistSuggestions directly on a directServer and bounds elapsed time; the 1 ns case drives POST /api/v1/issues/{key}/asks through the real route table with the write-advice query failing, and asserts the envelope the filer receives. Different surface, and it is the case the spec names. Its cost is one database clone.
